question: Should Discord subagent progress become a supported configuration and channel lifecycle capability after the mechanical defects are fixed?
rationale: Correctness work cannot decide whether OpenClaw should permanently support seven new Discord settings, public requester message metadata, a channel lifecycle adapter, and persisted presentation-cleanup state.

options.title: Sponsor after fixes
options.body: Accept the opt-in feature after nested override semantics, current-main conflicts, and exact-head proof are resolved.

options.title: Narrow the permanent surface
options.body: Keep the visible Discord behavior but reduce tuning fields or cross-core lifecycle API exposure before merge.

options.title: Decline the feature direction
options.body: Close the PR if Discord-specific progress does not justify the added configuration and lifecycle contracts.

recommendation.title: Sponsor after fixes
recommendation.body: Accept the opt-in feature after nested override semantics, current-main conflicts, and exact-head proof are resolved.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent ownership of subagent/session persistence makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the cross-core lifecycle and stored-state decision.
